decisions.evidence: Disassembly plus bounded x64 emulation with inert Windows API stubs independently reaches FindWindowA(Shell_TrayWnd), GetWindowThreadProcessId, OpenProcess(0x1fffff), VirtualAllocEx(MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE), WriteProcessMemory of a mapped PE64 image and CreateRemoteThread at an appended bootstrap. The static rule binds allocation/write handle slots and the concrete indirect-call argument blocks, with TLS flattening and dynamic API resolution.
decisions.limitations: No host process or network operation occurred. Handles, PID and DLL metadata were supplied by inert stubs. The captured mapped image has analysis-stub import addresses and is not a pristine on-disk payload. Payload internals and family attribution are not claimed.

decisions.evidence: Automatic bounded MPRESS LZMA recovery reproduces the independently recovered service/client hashes and scans the children. Bounded PE version-resource fallback recovers the client product claim despite the full parser resource-size guard. The remote-control implementation plus contradictory Disk Manager product identity triggers hostile on both client and wrapper. Earlier independent configuration decoding and Rizin analysis remain corroborating evidence.
decisions.limitations: No Grandoreiro family attribution or endpoint contact. Genuine RdViewer service remains neutral. Automatic recovery supports the recognized MPRESS x86 LZMA stub with explicit size/tree/depth limits, not every MPRESS variant.

decisions.evidence: Emulated isolated native literal constructors: 1362 decoded outputs expose browser Login Data/cookies, wallets, cloud credential caches, .git-credentials, AI-tool configuration and CredentialManager output. Followed browser-pointer construction and collection/endpoint-string callers in disassembly. Added a narrow hostile composite for the actual profile-pointer array plus dense keyed literal builders.
decisions.limitations: No remote traffic or full application execution; not every collector/upload branch was fully recovered. VT 10 detections is corroboration, not the reason for this verdict.

decisions.evidence: Fully decoded and inspected. Hidden, borderless ScriptExecutor HTA with an empty VBScript block. There are no concealed executable script bytes to recover. An endpoint engineer should lean suspicious/malicious remnant and retain it for investigation.
decisions.limitations: Insufficient payload to establish hostile behavior; deliberately excluded from good training data.

decisions.evidence: Read every archive member. Postinstall generates a temporary package manifest, hides its command word behind printf expansion, and removes the temporary directory. This variant reconstructs an invalid publish command; the failure does not make the install-hook abuse benign. Added hostile compound detection.
decisions.limitations: The command as written does not successfully publish. No credential theft was found; no lifecycle hook executed.

decisions.evidence: Read every archive member. Postinstall creates a temporary package manifest, reconstructs npm publish with printf, implicitly publishes using the installation environment, and removes the directory. Concealment and unwanted publish-on-install justify bad despite proof-of-concept framing.
decisions.limitations: No credential theft claimed; no lifecycle hook executed.

decisions.limitations: Final payload not fully unpacked; Remcos/AutoIt engine labels are not adopted as proven family attribution.

decisions.evidence: Independent native main disassembly ties own-image reading to random mutation, writing a generated clone, multipart file upload, deletion and repeat branches. New rules bind the shared buffer, size, filename and libcurl call targets. Hostile detection survives removal of the campaign banner and destination URL.
decisions.limitations: Historical deployment used an opt-in malware VM playground. The rule detects autonomous mutated self-submission; it does not claim unauthorized remote execution, infection of host files or theft. Rifaien identity remains separately neutral.

decisions.evidence: Built a newer innoextract and recovered the complete application tree. All extracted member scans have no suspicious or hostile traits. Eight VT installer hits share the MSILHeracles adware signature; no independent adware mechanism was recovered.
decisions.limitations: This is an evidence-based likely false positive, not proof of universal safety. Main application EXE/DLL hash lookups returned 404 (unknown). Future server-delivered content and operator/business trust are outside the reviewed bytes.
